blocks.text:
In the morning, you will head to the station at the foot of Corcovado.

A train takes you up through the Tijuca Forest. Through the windows, you can see dense vegetation, vines, damp tree trunks and large tropical leaves. As you climb, the city almost disappears behind the greenery before opening up again from above.

At the summit stands the statue of Christ the Redeemer. Up close, its scale feels quite different from photographs or the view from Sugar Loaf. From the observation deck, almost the whole of Rio unfolds before you.

Sugar Loaf, Guanabara Bay, the Botanical Garden, the Maracanã Stadium and the neighbourhoods around the lagoon are clearly visible. Corcovado gives a particularly clear sense of how the city fits between mountains, forest and water.

After the tour, you can spend the evening as you wish. Return to the ocean, stroll along the promenade or choose one of the city's cafés. After a night at the Sambadrome, this quieter day offers another view of the city, away from the Carnival rush.

blocks.text: Rio de Janeiro – Foz do Iguaçu

provenance.wordAbsenceReason: The Word Day 5 paragraph names the flight endpoints but has no standalone route title.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, transfer to the airport for your flight to Foz do Iguaçu.

Within a few hours, the surroundings change completely. Rio is left behind, along with its beaches, dense city streets and Carnival music. Iguazu welcomes you with humid air, lush greenery and a very different natural setting.

On arrival, you will be met and transferred to your selected hotel. Use the rest of the day to relax before 2 full days of excursions to the falls.

Foz do Iguaçu is a convenient base for exploring the complex. The next day, you will see the broad panorama from the Brazilian side, then cross the border to follow the Argentine walkways closer to the cascades.

The domestic flight Rio de Janeiro – Iguazu is charged separately. Prices start from USD 250.
